Odin × Godot

Optional SDK host protocol

6 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Code, data and scene contextShared request and reservation accounting

protocol.h and protocol.odin define the same C-shaped records. The protocol package imports no native backend, framework, Godot objects, allocator or typeid. Importing Owner/Status activates no native profile. Core's implementation is in host/; the optional producer-side retained allocator is in meter/.

The public ABI is version 1: Owner 48 bytes, Data_Lease 24, Capsule 32 and Service 200 on the supported 64-bit targets. protocol_fingerprint() covers actual sizes, alignments and offsets; the independent C reference is in tests/box3d_modules/core/protocol_test.c.

Runtime exports pure odin_scripts_box3d_profile, odin_scripts_box3d_protocol and odin_scripts_box3d_contract, and an installation entry odin_scripts_box3d_install. A native binding registers discovery/install with module_register; optional adapters register pure realm installers with module_add_hook. Install hooks configure guards/realms only; they must not create resources or invoke authored code. Core validates before boot, creates a producer record once its existing Script_Generation exists, then installs before instances can use it. Hook installation publishes the module Service only after all hooks succeed. Every opted-in SDK module must explicitly declare even profile 0; older modules cannot evade admission by omitting the handshake.

BOX3D_HOST_ENABLED=true enables the Core service. Root's build/deployment code supplies BOX3D_NATIVE_LIBRARY, copies the verified shared backend beside Core as libogb3.dylib/libogb3.so, and supplies controlled consumer loader paths. Core resolves that exact adjacent filename; it does not search a runtime environment override. Scripts use BOX3D_REQUIRE_DOMAIN=true and the verified BOX3D_EXPECTED_BUILD=sha256:<64hex> and BOX3D_EXPECTED_TARGET=sha256:<64hex>. The explicit prefix prevents Odin command line numeric inference from truncating hashes such as 9e41bb...; comparison strips only that prefix and still requires exactly 32 digest bytes. Discovery and binding installation compare these compile expectations and the actual native cookie; an older mapped ABI-compatible library cannot silently satisfy a new build. The cookie and producer realm are process-local lifetime capabilities, never Game, network, recovery or durable identity. Standalone/default native-free framework behavior remains available without this service.

Code, data and scene context#

An Owner retains its existing SDK generation independently of its data context. Its check/retain/drop functions point into stable Core. The consumer checks its module-local realm before any typed object, allocator or type metadata access, then calls Core's protected-origin check. A different producer or reload realm requires a C capsule or canonical conversion, even when nominal types match. Native-profile script_of/script_any also reject a raw typed userdata handoff across producer generations; ordinary non-native targets keep their existing behavior.

Data_Lease callbacks retain an actual managed heap/allocator context. They must be paired, have atomic failure behavior, and belong to the originating loaded code image (or the known stable Core same-producer Owner hook pair). They do not make arbitrary raw pointers owned. Strict factories reject unsupported borrowed allocators/users, validate exact declared context pointers or explicit retained allocation-block aliases, and use the SDK meter for participating containers. Source scene userdata and its subfields cannot be claimed by a Data_Lease; Core checks their registered allocation spans before invoking retain callbacks.

context_caps contains MANAGED_DATA=1 plus WEAK_INSTANCE=2 or INDEPENDENT_CONTEXT=4. READ=0 permits cached reads, clones and destruction under the origin. EXECUTE=1 additionally requires the captured weak scene instance to remain live. A weak declaration cannot retain raw self. Logical invalidation precedes actual source free; context_release closes the physical span only after its userdata allocation is freed. Detached weak owners retain a tombstone until their final drop. New instance/reload contexts are bound before any new setter/default/reload callback runs. Retained data and code can therefore support cached operations after actual scene destruction while authored execution fails.

Capsule data stays opaque outside its producer. Creation validates and stores the origin C dispatcher while the caller is protected. Capsule.invoke and Capsule.destroy enter stable Core, acquire the existing execution gate and a temporary generation pin, establish the origin, and invoke the whole typed operation. That includes fields, events, allocator frees and accounting. The producer callback returns into Core before the call pin and gate are released. Last release schedules the existing writer-gate collector; no producer-local leave-and-return wrapper substitutes for this outer boundary.

Operations 0 (destroy) and 1 (clone with Capsule_Clone_Args) are common. Other operation argument records require the producer's separately agreed C-shaped interface; no typed framework object/allocator/typeid crosses an opaque args pointer. Wrong origin/thread and invalid handles reject before dispatch. A valid data release is expected to succeed; if its atomic drop declines after a payload destructor, Core retains a cleanup-only tombstone, denies reads and retries only the final lease drop, never the freed payload destructor.

Shared request and reservation accounting#

Core uses the one native ledger. Fixed bounded Core registry storage is charged once. Each producer has ONE aggregate LIVE plus remaining-reservation token; category publishers report actual live bytes and monotonic successful HOST requests. Forecast admission sizes are not observed live storage. Successful requests remain counted after frees, reallocations or admission failure. The native engine and snapshot-wrapper requested counters are observed once, and all producer HOST requests participate in the cumulative operation observer. Metadata/allocator table costs must also be charged. Covered SDK allocations must not be counted again by old manual provider/Core estimates.

Each successful budget_begin returns a unique mark. A same-producer child compares its declared bound with the outer ORIGINAL bound, shares the remaining promise and adds no ticket. Actual cumulative requests consume that promise; net-live differences never substitute. Another producer's allocation budget or increasing account while one is active returns Unsupported before mutation. Cached cross-producer reads remain allowed. An allocating A capsule clone under caller B is allowed when B has no active allocation budget.

budget_reconcile never ends a mark. Exactly one deferred cleanup owns each successful begin. budget_end accepts only the top unique mark; duplicates, stale IDs and ending a parent while a child exists return InvalidHandle without popping anything. A valid end returning Capacity still ends that mark and releases its promise; clear the caller's mark and abort the candidate, never retry the end or accidentally end its parent.

legacy_extra(user,0,0,proposed_extra,out) reconciles first. Within an active budget, the proposed request must fit remaining and is already covered; the result includes all registered LIVE plus remaining reservations once. Outside a budget it additionally counts the unregistered extra. It excludes native engine/wrapper bytes because the legacy native/alpha check adds those once.

An explicit current mark plus implicit_C_reserve excludes only the held portion of that operation's promise, up to min(implicit,remaining). Native C still adds its FULL implicit reserve; any gap is conservative, never a skipped check or another producer's stolen ticket. An ancestor and child cannot both exclude an implicit reserve. For opaque custom recovery catalogs, read holds a 6 MiB operation bound but excludes only the guaranteed native 4 MiB staging floor; C still checks actual DTO limit plus 4 MiB. A known exact configured DTO limit permits its exact DTO+4 MiB exception. Write retains its 8 MiB operation preflight and all original resource/semantic/codec validation.

Core uses its existing reader/writer gate and generation references. The alpha host supports one main-thread caller; other threads return Unsupported before native/typed owner use. Core shutdown refuses live native/typed owners and never force-frees them. It closes the registry charge only after all producer/data owners are gone. This service is not an allocator hard cap or recovery from the native engine's fatal OOM boundary.

Actual Godot two-module/reload acceptance belongs to the coordinator. C/fake-gate controls alone do not certify it. The separate cold editor-import failure in Godot 4.7.1 is recorded with original-binary cold/warm controls and LLDB evidence; it has no SDK workaround or accepted cold-import pass here. The declared macOS reference Gate B is recorded separately in docs/design/box3d/gate-b.md; functional host tests alone do not establish CPU or whole-application performance.
